name: http-request
description: Make outbound HTTP requests to external APIs. EGRESS: allowed_hosts is ["*"], so this module's own host grant places no restriction on which host it reaches - the destination is whatever the node's config resolves to. What still constrains it: the worker's SSRF resolver (private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused), the bound actor's egress_scope (scope 'local' refuses public egress outright), and max_llm_tier (a tier1 actor is refused every external LLM host regardless of allowed_hosts). To pin this node to specific hosts, install a private copy and narrow allowed_hosts with update_module_hosts.

METHOD.description: The HTTP method. Default GET. The installed copy's allowed_methods must include it.

URL.description: The URL to request. Its host must be one the installed copy is granted (allowed_hosts).

HEADERS.description: Request headers, as a list of {key, value}. A value written as a vault:// reference is replaced by the platform with the secret, never seen by the module, and only when the copy is granted that secret and the URL's host is named in its allowed_hosts ("*" names no host).

BODY.description: The request body, sent as written (for POST, PUT and PATCH).

TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long to wait for the response, in milliseconds. Default 5000.

SANITIZE_FOR_LLM.description: When true, sanitizes the HTTP response for safe LLM consumption: strips HTML tags, enforces MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH, and wraps the result in [EXTERNAL_CONTENT_BEGIN]...[EXTERNAL_CONTENT_END] delimiters so the LLM can distinguish external content from instructions.

MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH.description: Maximum byte length of the response body when SANITIZE_FOR_LLM is true. Content beyond this limit is truncated with a [TRUNCATED] marker before being passed to downstream nodes. Default: 8192 bytes.

MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES.description: Maximum bytes of the raw response body to return, applied whether or not SANITIZE_FOR_LLM is set. Use it when the next node is an extractor that needs the raw body but the body may exceed the platform's node-input limit (about 1 MB). The cut is walked back to a character boundary. Unset: the body is not truncated.
